priorities.title: Grammar precision in spontaneous speech
priorities.why: Louise can sustain complex conversation, but accuracy becomes less stable while she is formulating longer ideas in real time.
priorities.evidence: March portfolio focus areas and recurrent tense, comparative, preposition and sentence-framing issues in the August transcript.

priorities.title: Lexical precision and retrieval
priorities.why: Her conceptual range is broad; the next gain is faster access to precise English with less word-searching and Portuguese transfer.
priorities.evidence: August discussion repeatedly triggered useful lexical work around social inequality, household, cost of living, public transport and cultural events.

priorities.title: Structured extended opinions
priorities.why: Louise already has strong ideas and reflective depth. Clearer framing and sequencing will make complex arguments easier to follow.
priorities.evidence: Extended August discussion across politics, inclusion, public policy, economics, transport and culture.

nextAction.outcome: Deliver a structured three-minute opinion while maintaining fluency and improving precision.
nextAction.title: Current Affairs Precision Round
nextAction.description: Choose one meaningful topic and give a three-minute opinion with a clear opening position, two supporting reasons and a conclusion. Reuse at least three active vocabulary items and prioritize complete sentence framing while keeping the delivery natural.
nextAction.evidence: The latest transcript shows that Louise performs best in substantive discussion and that precision, rather than basic communication, is the most useful next step.

grammarOverview.title: Grammar Overview (Cumulative)
grammarOverview.summary: Louise communicates effectively in extended spontaneous conversation. The priority is precision under cognitive load rather than elementary grammar coverage.
focusPoints: Improve consistency when moving between past experiences and present meaning.
Use comparative forms more accurately and naturally.
Strengthen verb patterns such as need to, prefer to and decide to.
Complete sentence frames more consistently during long explanations.
Use reformulation and recasting inside meaningful conversation rather than isolated drills.
